title: Paid after a tax exemption or charity registration was lost
question: Which organizations did the City go on paying after a State or federal list shows their exemption revoked or their charity registration not current?
finding: 9 City payees share a name and city with an entry on the State tax board's list of revoked exemptions and were paid afterwards, $28.8 million in all; the list carries no employer number, so each is a name-and-city match: the records do not show whether the listed entity and the City’s payee are the same organization or two with the same name, and the State entity number would settle it. The largest: United Playaz Inc. (listed 2008-10-30, $20.9 million since); Excelsior Action Group (listed 2021-08-20, $3.2 million since); Freedom West Homes Corporation (listed 2019-04-02, $1.8 million since); Asian Pacific Islander Cultural Center (listed 2016-08-25, $1.6 million since). 2 organizations matched by employer number are on the Attorney General's may-not-operate list and were paid in fiscal 2026 or 2027 ($4.6 million). 3 lost the federal exemption for not filing and regained it under a new ruling; 0 with no later ruling in the master file were paid afterwards.
how: The download of regulator lists already matched to City suppliers (the “status matches” table) is read again with the dates: the Franchise Tax Board's complete list of revoked exempt organizations, the IRS automatic revocation list and the Attorney General's list of charities that may not operate or solicit. Federal and Attorney General rows are used only on an exact employer-number match. The State tax board's list has no employer number, so its rows are exact-name matches in the same city and are worded as unconfirmed. City payments are summed for fiscal years after the listed date; for a federal revocation followed by a new ruling in the IRS master file, for the fiscal years touching the gap.
limits: the “standing” analysis shows current standing for profiled nonprofits on employer-number matches; because the State tax board's list has no employer number, none of its rows had reached the site. A revoked State exemption makes an organization taxable in California; it does not by itself bar a City grant, and the list does not say whether the exemption was later restored. An old federal revocation followed by a new ruling usually means late returns that were then filed. The State entity number printed in each row, looked up at the Secretary of State or the tax board, settles whether the entry is the City's payee.
